correctness.rationale: The D4 Voronoi region is proved to be the convex hull of exactly 24 unit vertices, of four-volume 2. A dot-product extremality argument places every squared-radius superlevel above 3/4 in a disjoint union of 24 congruent vertex caps. In each cap x=(1-t,tu), the exact squared-radius deficit is 2t-(1+sum u_i^2)t^2, monotone up to t=1/4; an exact Jacobian integral gives the full asserted CDF on 0<epsilon<1/4. Lagrange inversion and uniform convergence yield the full coefficient formula. The compiled local verifier checked exact rational coefficients, discrete symmetry and geometric bounds, and numerical quadrature versus 1.2 million exact-law volume-uniform samples.

originality.rationale: The claim determines the exact endpoint radial CDF, on an entire interval, for the unscaled D4 24-cell. Liu establishes second-moment global optimality, Conway–Sloane computes mean-square moments, and Ordentlich provides random-lattice CDF bounds and points to earlier plotted D4 radial functions. None of these inspected statements establishes the exact 3-cube cap formula with the full positive rational endpoint series. Public geometry-index results on a regular 24-cell width distribution and regular-simplex nearest-vertex tail are different statistics/objects. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An older paper is cited as having evaluated/plotted the D4 radial function; its full technical content was not accessible here. Exact endpoint expressions could have been overlooked under different terminology.
The full text of the listed public regular-simplex tail record was inaccessible; its summary covers a distinct geometric domain. This alone does not establish unconditional historical priority.
The proof is analytic, but no independent audit or archival literature exhaustion has been performed.

value.rationale: The full tail near covering radius for the canonical 24-cell Voronoi region quantifies near-worst lattice-quantization error, independent information from mean-square distortion. It determines a natural interval-exact probability law, the fourth-order critical tail, and all higher strictly positive rational coefficients via an explicit nontrivial cap decomposition. It is neither an arbitrary finite enumeration nor only a normalization check.
